title: Serilog
description: Serilog is the most popular structured logging library for .NET. Unlike traditional logging libraries that write plain text, Serilog stores events as structured data, making it easy to query and analyze logs.

data.text: Serilog provides structured logging for .NET applications. Instead of writing plain text messages, Serilog stores each log event as structured data with named properties. This makes it easy to filter, search, and analyze logs in tools like Seq, Elasticsearch, or Splunk.

data.title: Installation
data.content: Install the core Serilog package and a sink.
data.code:
dotnet add package Serilog
dotnet add package Serilog.Sinks.Console

data.title: Basic Serilog Setup
data.content: Configure Serilog in Program.cs with a console sink.

terms.definition: Logging that captures events as data objects with named properties rather than plain text strings.
A destination where Serilog writes log events, such as Console, File, Seq, or Elasticsearch.
A log message format with named placeholders like {Name} that Serilog captures as structured properties.

data.title: Why Structured Logging?
data.text: With structured logging, you can query for all events where FreeSpace < 20 instead of parsing text. Tools like Seq let you filter and visualize these properties instantly.

Serilog writes structured events to a sink — console, file, Seq, Elasticsearch. Enrichers add ambient data such as the machine name, the thread id, or the current request id, so every event carries the same context. The `UseSerilogRequestLogging` middleware turns each HTTP request into one structured completion event.

data.title: A configured host with a request-logging middleware
One completion event beats many start/end pairs
data.text: A middleware that logs "request started" and "request finished" doubles the volume and is hard to correlate. `UseSerilogRequestLogging` emits a single event with the path, status, and elapsed time at completion, which is what you actually query on. Structured properties on that event are what make a log backend useful.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Serilog captures logs as structured data, not plain text
Sinks define where logs are written
Message templates preserve property names for querying
data.takeaway: Serilog turns logging from a debugging afterthought into a searchable, analyzable data source.

data.title: Exercise: Set Up Serilog
data.description: Create a console app that logs structured events using Serilog.
steps: Create a new console project with dotnet new console
Add the Serilog and Serilog.Sinks.Console packages
Configure Serilog to write to the console with a JSON formatter
Log an Information event with a UserId and Action property
Log a Warning event with an ErrorCode property
Run the app and observe the structured output
data.expectedOutcome: Console output shows each log event as JSON with named properties that can be filtered and searched.
